sources.title: University of Washington Silk Road exhibition: The Khitan and the Liao Dynasty
sources.note: Directly read paragraphs on Shi Jingtang, Khitan assistance, Sixteen Prefectures and later Song recovery attempts. Uses only these bounded political facts; does not adopt other broad cultural generalizations.

sources.title: Old History of the Five Dynasties, chapter 79
sources.note: Primary received court history, later compilation, modern digital transcription. Directly checked Tianfu fifth year, first, third, fourth and fifth/sixth lunar-month entries. Decrees establish official intentions, not proof of uniform implementation.

sources.title: Ouyang Xiu: New History of the Five Dynasties, chapter 9
sources.note: Later Song-period primary historiography, modern digital transcription. Directly read succession, 943 locust response, 944-946 war and final military surrender; Gregorian fall is January 947 although annals place it in the preceding Chinese year. Combined work budget with chapter 17.

sources.title: Ouyang Xiu: New History of the Five Dynasties, chapter 17
sources.note: Directly read Li empress biography and captive royal household. Physician, seven cooks and three tea/wine attendants in exile list; hardship and gathering wild plants later. Same-work budget combined with chapter 9.

sources.title: Taiyuan Institute of Archaeology: Excavation report of the Later Jin tomb at Jinci, Wenwu 2018(2), pp. 4-10
sources.note: Directly read complete mirrored original archaeological report, not the hosting account as historical authority. Original institutional authorship and journal bibliography independently confirmed by Paris Musées catalogue https://parismuseescollections.paris.fr/en/node/652769. Figures 3, 5 and 14; epitaph transcription and concluding identity discussion. Excavated 2005, burial dated 937. Relationship of Wang to Guo Zhimi explicitly unknown.

sources.title: Changzhi Daily visual centre: Pingshun Dayunyuan, 18 October 2024, p. 6
sources.note: Government-hosted original newspaper PDF, full article available through indexed original; direct PDF open failed. Reproducible query site.changzhi.gov.cn "千年古刹大云院" "938". Foundation 938, surviving Five Dynasties Amitabha hall, murals and raised gilding. Other sources distinguish hall completion 940; prose dates foundation only, not every timber or mural.

sources.title: National Museum of China: Coins of the Five Dynasties
sources.note: Direct museum description read: Tianfu Yuanbao diameter 2.2 cm, dynastic issues circulated alongside Tang coins.

sources.title: University of Shanghai for Science and Technology: Old Book of Tang
sources.note: Institutional indexed original checked with site.deyu.usst.edu.cn "旧唐书" "945". Direct page redirects to error. Indexed text confirms completion 945 and 200 juan, authors close enough to Tang to access earlier records. Does not use disputed commission year.

proposedOverrides.name: Later Jin
proposedOverrides.summary: A northern Five Dynasties court, 936-947, with printing, historical compilation and an alliance that reshaped its northern frontier.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Exact indexed ID only. Distinct from jin-dynasty, Jurchen jin-dynasty-1115, Later Tang and Later Han; no aliases added.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: borders/china-seams.geojson, site-created coarse polygon, bbox [102,32,122,40], dates 936-947. Same extent later reused for Later Han; this does not establish dynastic identity. Feature excludes Sixteen Prefectures; note dates cession to 938, while foundation alliance and commitment belong to 936. Public text avoids equating every procedural date.
batchIdentityNotes.chronology: Index historical span 936-947 retained. Shi Jingtang 936-942 and Shi Chonggui 942-947. Final Chinese-year annals entry translates to January 947, not a 946 historical ending. No exact point date added to undated material objects.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Lady Wang epitaph M1:11, 937, original Wenwu 2018 archaeological report mirrored online and bibliographically verified independently. Eight-character wish quoted. Modern traditional typography and Mandarin pinyin explicitly labelled. Unknown relationship of Wang to commissioner Guo preserved.
batchIdentityNotes.limits: Court decrees and later chronicles identified as such. No universal diet, schooling, medical service or sanitation system inferred. Tea/medicine concerns officials; exile staff concerns royal household. Tomb goods are burial furnishings. Temple foundation 938 distinguished from surviving hall and mural dating.
